findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed TCS foods not being cold held below 41 F in a broken prep cooler. CORRECTED: PIC and staff discarded TCS food items that were inside the prep cooler if they were prepared longer than 4 hours ago, and TCS items prepared under 4 hours were moved to a working cooler. This cooler cannot be used for service unless it is repaired (see Violation #33) or a Time as Control Policy is created and used. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at temperatures of 41 F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed that the prep cooler on the far end of the kitchen by the office was still observed not keeping the appropriate temperature range. The average temperature within the cooler using the infrared thermometer was 55F. Temperatures obtained by probing was 45F. PICs previously told Inspector that the unit will be repaired accordingly, but per PICs they are still waiting on a part. Cease using the prep cooler for cold holding until it is repaired. Ensure that the necessary repairs are done enabling the unit to have the appropriate temperature capacity.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was provided and the behavior was corrected.  Ensure that employees are reminded to always properly wash their hands before donning gloves in between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple items to be held past their seven day date mark (gyro meat- 10/31, salsa ranch- 10/27, and chipotle BBQ-10/27). CORRECTED- the gyro meat was discarded, and the PIC stated the other sauces had been remade since the sticker date, and the items were re-stickered with the correct dates. Ensure all Time/Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) food items are marked with the date they are prepared, and are used or discarded within seven days. The day of preparation or thawing counts as day one. To help ensure this practice takes place, ensure sauces are placed into a new container that has been clean and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The PIC stated their Allergen Awareness Certificate had expired, and they were unable to produce Allergen Awareness certificates for any Certified Food Protection Managers (CFM/CFPM). Inspector provided Allergen Awareness literature to the PIC, which included a web address to ANSI-accredited institutes. Ensure all CFMs obtain an Allergen Awareness certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text:

Ensure staff provide copies of current food handler certifications by the next routine inspection. Staff need to complete a food handler course within 30 days from date of hire. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

10 tiles located in front of fryers observed damaged and grease/dirt is accumulating within the cracks. Discussed with PIC. Will follow up at next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 & 2-301.15 While speaking with the employee in dish area about handwashing between tasks, the employee stated he wipes his hands on a blue wiping cloth to dry his hands and between handling soiled and clean dishes. Employee demonstrated by wiping hands on the cloth towel. Employee was advised to cease the practice and to wash hands prior to handling clean dishes. Employee asked if he could wash hands at the 3 part sink and was advised he must wash hands at the designated handsink only. Cross-contamination concern was briefly discussed, and blue wiping cloth was placed in the soiled linen bag. 
 Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Ensure hands are properly washed between handling soiled and clean equipment and utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11 Employee was observed ringing out a wiping cloth in the handsink. Proper use of handsinks was discussed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Ensure designated handsinks in the kitchen and bar are used for handwashing and no other purpose.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.13 Hand soap dispenser was observed at the 3 part sink in the dish area. Remove the hand soap dispenser from the dish area.
All sinks not used for handwashing should not be supplied with handwashing aids/devices.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Baffle in ice machine at south wait station was soiled with mold buildup. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup.
Equipment with enclosed components such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

6-501.12 Dust buildup was observed on the HVAC air exchange vent cover above the kitchen handsink. Some chunks of dust were hanging from the cover. Clean the vent covers as needed to minimize buildup. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11 Cologne was observed on a shelf in the dry storage area. Kitchen manager placed cologne in the office for storage. 
Sunglasses were observed in a container located in the prep area with a thermometer and wet wipes. Kitchen manager discarded sunglasses. 
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket in back of kitchen was less than 100ppm quat. Sani-buckets were remade with quat solution that was mixed by hand after removing the chemical from the dispenser. Manually mixed solutions were observed at 200ppm quat. Call for service was made to check and repair the chemical dispenser.
Dish machine was at 0ppm chlorine. Lines were primed and concentration was still at 0ppm. Call for service was made to check and repair the dish machine. Manually wash, rinse, and sanitize dishes until machine is working properly.
NOTE: 5 gal buckets were used to combine chemical from 1 gal jugs since last routine inspection in 2019. Kitchen manager will have technician convert the machine to be using 1 gal jugs of product again and ensure chemical lines are suctioning properly. 
Spot check will be conducted on 5/13/20 to verify proper function of chemical dispenser and dish machine. 
*Ensure disposable wiping cloths in 360 Solutions container are maintained in solution at proper concentration.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Personal beverage in an uncovered Styrofoam cup was observed on the lower shelf beneath the grill. Manager discarded the beverage. Ensure proper storage of personal beverages.
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

Bar manager was chewing gum. Manager discarded gum at request of inspector. 
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Server was observed washing hands without proper technique in the kitchen. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper technique was discussed. 

To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival inspector observed knives in the kitchen handsink and a crate with a working supply of lettuce on ice was in front of the handsink. Knives were placed in dish area and crate was moved to allow access to the handsink. Proper use and accessibility of handsinks were discussed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Two of the three food thermometers available for use in the kitchen had varying amounts of grease/food debris stuck on the stem. Thermometers were cleaned during inspection. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or sanitizer are used to wipe stems between temperature checks, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of eggroll sauce were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 70F-75F on the prep table across from the salad cooler. Portions of salsa and sour cream in the same area were also at 70F. Portions were discarded. 
--Pitchers of dressings were out on the prep table across from the salad cooler. Ranch and blue cheese dressings were observed with internal temperatures of 57F and 76F respectively. All pitchers of dressing that were out in the salad area were discarded. A time control policy was established for working supplies of dressings/sauces held at room temperature during lunch and dinner service. 
--Working supply of lettuce stored in a stock pot on ice had surface temperatures at 46F-51F and internal temperatures of 46F-48F. Cold holding was discussed with emphasis on using a larger container for the ice bath to allow for submersion during storage. Portion of lettuce was placed in the walkin cooler for storage. 
--Pans containing portions of Italian beef, chicken wings, raw chicken strips, raw stuffed chicken, and eggrolls were held in a pan that was sitting within another pan containing ice. This is a new practice that started recently for storage of working supplies of these foods during lunch and dinner service. Internal temperatures were observed at 46F-59F depending on how much product was present and how foods were stocked in pans. All foods were placed out for service at 11:45am and were to be used or discarded by 5:45pm since foods were holding below 70F. A time control policy was established for these foods (see general comments). 
--TCS foods in the salad cooler were observed with temperatures at 52F-53F. Diced ham and turkey was checked in the top holding area and cottage cheese was checked in the bottom. Ice buildup was observed in the bottom of he unit (see #33). All TCS foods were discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Hanging thermometer in salad cooler was reading around 50F. All foods in the top and bottom were observed at temperatures above 50F. Ice accumulation was observed on the back wall in the bottom of the unit. Cooler was taken out of service. Cooler will be repaired or replaced. Do not use the cooler for long term storage of TCS foods. Use time control for working supplies of foods during service (serve/discard within 4-6hrs based on temperature during use - see time control policy for details). 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometers checked with ice water were observed reading above 34F. Thermometers were calibrated to 32F during inspection. Owner also purchased additional thermometers for use. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.citation_text:
2-303.11 Employee doing food prep was observed wearing a large watch. Watch was removed from wrist upon request of inspector.
Except for a plain ring such as a wedding band, while preparing food, food employees may not wear jewelry including medical information jewelry on their arms and hands.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Insulation and plumbing inside the wall were exposed under the kitchen 3 part sink. Options for repairs were discussed with the owner.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in food repair.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Kitchen manager with allergen awareness training had to leave and none of the other staff had proof of a current allergen certification. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Strainer was observed in the top of the far left compartment at the bar four part sink, indicating use a dump sink the evening prior. This compartment is designated for handwashing only and was stocked with handwashing supplies. Strainer was removed from the sink, and a dump bucket was provided. All staff were advised on proper use of the sink. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the left compartment at the bar four part sink as a dump sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Final rinse concentration for the dish machine was 0ppm chlorine. An empty sanitizer jug was located near the fresh jug that was likely hooked up the evening prior. After running several ware washing cycles and priming the sanitizer line the final rinse concentration was observed at 100ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 The stem of one food thermometer was observed with stuck on food debris. Thermometer was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. Proper use and maintenance of thermometers were discussed. Food thermometers need to be cleaned after use and prior to storage.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Foods located in the bottom of the cook line prep cooler were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 48F-54F. These foods were located in the middle section of the cooler and included salad greens, chicken skewers, pork, and blue cheese portions. Other foods in the bottom of the cooler on the far ends had internal temperatures at 43F, and foods in the top were at 40F-41F. TCS foods above 43F were discarded. 
The middle gasket was observed to be severely damaged causing the door to not shut properly on the cooler (see #47 for details). 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish portions were in the process of thawing in the walkin cooler at the time of inspection. Directions on the packaging states to remove vacuum packaging before thawing. At least one portion was fully thawed while others were still frozen. Management was advised to make sure the packaging removed prior to thawing. 
Frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 & 4-501.11 Middle door on the bottom of the cook line prep cooler was not shutting properly due to a damaged gasket. The right door was slightly askew on the bottom, and the topper with hinged lids had an area of disrepair on the left end that had duct tape on it. Manager on duty stated gaskets and a new hinged lid topper were ordered to replace parts in question (w/in ~30 days). In the meantime, no TCS foods should be held in the cooler beyond use during hours of operation. Store foods in the walkin cooler overnight until repairs are completed. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
Equipment components such as doors, seals, and hinges shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-603.12 An old label was observed on a pan containing portions of sliced ham in the walkin cooler. The date on the label said 9/5, but the ham was sliced on 9/15 based on a label for fat filler also located in the pan. Old label was removed. 
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives. Ensure that labels are removed and all surfaces of pans are getting properly cleaned and sanitized between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Fryers were observed with buildup of grease on the sides, underneath surfaces, and in the lower compartment where mechanicals are located. Clean the fryers.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Old sani-bucket containing sanitizer solution from the evening prior was observed on the cook line alongside a fresh sani-bucket. The old solution was discarded. Ensure sanitizer solutions are emptied throughout the day as needed and at the end of operations daily. 
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Walls in the dish area under the dish machine and 3 part sink were soiled with splash/general buildup. The plumbing under the 3 part sink was also soiled.
In addition, insulation and plumbing inside the wall under the 3 part sink were exposed due to recent repairs. Clean the walls and repair the wall in the dish area. 

Floors under ice machines were soiled with general debris. Clean the floors under the ice machines.

Floor under/behind fryers was soiled with grease and food debris. The floor was also damaged and holding grease where tiles were damaged. Clean under the fryers and repair damaged tiles.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Barrier was not used to shut off the manual faucet. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Employee was later observed using proper technique during handwashing. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed going between handling soiled and clean dishes without washing hands and also wiped his hands on a wiping cloth observed hanging from the corner of shelving in the dish area. Employee was advised on handwashing between handling the soiled and cleaned dishes and to also cease the practice of wiping hands on cloth towels. Soiled wiping cloth was placed in laundry bag, and the employee washed his hands prior to continuing dish washing tasks. 
Food employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 Soufflé cup was observed as a scoop in marinara. Cup was removed and discarded during inspection.
Food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of milk in the walkin cooler had use by date of 4/17 and no date mark. The gallon of milk in question was discarded. Another open gallon of milk used to make chocolate milk with syrup in house was not labeled but was not past the product use by date. Person in charge provided a proper date mark for the chocolate milk.  
Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Caddies used for storage of clean utensils in the dish area were soiled with food crumbs. Clean the storage caddies daily/as needed, and maintain them clean to protect clean utensils from potential contamination.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Soiled cardboard was observed as lining on the shelf used for storage of milk in the walkin cooler. PIC noted it is used to keep the smaller jugs of milk from falling over and breaking in the cooler. Use of a cleanable alternative, such as a baking sheet, was discussed. 
Nonfood-contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) box fan in dish area (dusty); 
B) speed rails at the bar (general splash/buildup);   and
C) top ledge of beer coolers used for cup storage (debris/splash under liners). 
Clean the aforementioned items. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Half of the employees had expired food handler certifications. Owner sent information at the time of inspection to all staff that needed to renew certifications. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 PIC has not yet completed online food allergen awareness training. PIC was aware he needs the certification and is in the process of completing the course. 
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 - Pulled pork in a hot holding unit had surface and internal temperatures of 118°F and 140°F respectively. Cook in charge of reheat process stated he began reheating the pork around 7a, and the product was ~100°F when placed in the counter top hot holding unit. Temperature was checked by inspector at ~1010a. Food was beyond the 2hr time frame for rapid reheat. Pork was discarded, and a new bag was retrieved to heat for service. 

Foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be reheated rapidly to 165°F or higher throughout the product. Reheat process should be completed within 2hrs or less. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above.
NOTE: Use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to verify foods are reheated to 165°F/above within 2hrs.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment:
(R) 750.140 - Reach-in unit on the cook line that was formerly used as a freezer is now being utilized as a cooler. Foods in the unit were observed below 41°F, but a thermometer as not present in the cooler. Thermometers were purchased during the inspection, and one was placed in the cooler.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Pizza slicer on the magnetic knife strip at the end of the cook line was soiled with grease and food debris. Slicer was left on the cook line from the previous evening. Slicer was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Clean and sanitize the pizza slicer up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

Can opener blade and attached base were soiled with food debris. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Clean and sanitize the can opener blade up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

Lid containing old ranch dressing was stored with clean equipment. Lid was removed for cleaning. Properly clean and sanitize equipment between uses and prior to being stored in clean storage area.

Inside the dish machine and the contact tank for the sanitizer were starting to accumulate general buildup (grease/mold/food debris). Employee began cleaning the dish machine during the inspection. Clean the dish machine daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. 

Unwrapped piece of bread was observed sitting on the shelf in the reach-in cooler on the cook line. Bread was discarded in the trash. Store foods covered in clean containers between uses.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
(R) 750.160 - A soufflé cup was observed as a scoop in the marinara in the top holding area of the grill line prep cooler. Soufflé cup was removed and discarded during inspection.

Soufflé cup was also observed as a scoop in a container of cole slaw in the reach-in cooler on the cook line. The soufflé cup was discarded during inspection.

Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
(R) 750.510 & 1120 - Employee in dish area was observed wiping hands on a cloth towel. Towel was placed in soiled linen bin. Proper handwashing and use of disposable paper towels were discussed. Employee properly washed hands prior to retuning to work.

Employees were observed washing hands between tasks and glove changes; however, not all staff were utilizing proper technique. The same paper towel was used to continue drying hands after shutting off the faucet by one employee. Another employee shut off the manual faucet prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed with management and staff.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles. Common towels are prohibited and cannot be used to wipe hands for any reason.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
(R) 750.650a - Bulk flour storage bin lid has still not been replaced. A new lid has been ordered. 

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sani-buckets all tested at 100ppm quat. Solution was dispensed again for buckets from the wall mounted chemical unit, and the solution was constantly reading at 100ppm. A call for service was made. Prior to technician's arrival buckets were made using bleach (200ppm) and hand mixing quat solution (400ppm). GFS technician came and repaired the dispenser during the inspection. The solution was observed at 400ppm once the tip was changed in the unit. 

Maintain quat solution at 150-400ppm quat as indicated on label instructions. Use test strips to verify concentration of solutions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Upper ledge of the top cold holding area in the salad cooler was soiled with old food debris.

Shelves in the walkin cooler were soiled with buildup of mold and food splash.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1130 - Moldy waste water was observed under the 3 part sink. A leak is present in the plumbing, and a call for service was made during the inspection. The moldy waste water was discarded during the inspection.
NOTE: until the leak is repaired, make sure the container used as a catch basin is getting emptied and cleaned daily/as needed.

Liquid waste shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap and paper towels were not available at the area that should be designated for handwashing. 
Soap and paper towels were provided during inspection.

Maintain soap and paper towels at the far left sink of the 4 compartment sink to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were soiled in the following areas:
(R) A) under the ice machines (take home containers/food/general debris); 
B) far left corner at the bar (general debris);  and
C) dish area (grimy buildup).

Clean the floors under equipment and along floor to wall junctures daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Chicken breasts cooked within the hour and a half prior to inspector's arrival (based on information provided) had an internal temperature of 107°F. Product was not labeled with the time of prep/when cooling began. Chicken breasts were placed on a baking sheet in the walkin freezer to help rapidly chill foods. Internal temperature was at 30°F-31°F when checked later in the inspection. Another pan of chicken cooling in the walkin freezer that was pulled from the oven around 945a was not labeled. Other foods (rice, etc.) in the walkin cooler were labeled with the time.
Options for cooling to speed up the process and ensure proper cooling and labeling of cooling foods were discussed.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly/properly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Some foods in the grill prep cooler were observed above 45°F. Internal temperatures were as follows: cheese slices 47°F-48°F, mini burgers 54°F, deli meat portions 53°F, chicken 57°F-58°F, and burgers 53°F/57°F. All foods above 50°F were in the lower right reach-in section of the cooler, while cheese slices were in the upper right holding area. Meats and cheeses were discarded in the trash during inspection. Other products in the cooler were observed with internal temperatures of 42°F-45°F depending on where they were located and were kept for use. The gasket on the lower right door of the reach-in section was damaged and not allowing the door to seal properly. Kitchen Manager stated a new gasket was on order and checked with refrigeration technician during inspection. The gasket arrived the day prior, and the repairs would be completed later today. Until repairs were made, pans of ice would be utilized in the middle and lower right sides of the reach-in section to help hold foods cold. (See general comments)
 
Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Reach-in freezer on cook line was not holding at a temperature to keep foods frozen but was still maintaining foods below 41°F. Thermometer was not present, but inspector used stem thermometers to verify unit was between 30°F and 40°F. findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:

Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop was observed with handle down touching the ice in the machine on the south end of the bar. Ice scoop was positioned with handle out of the ice.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510, 512, & 1120 - Employee in dish area was observed wiping his hands on a cloth towel between handling dirty and clean dishes. Employee was advised on proper handwashing between tasks and to cease the use of cloth towels for wiping his hands. A roll of paper towels may be kept in the dish area for employees to wipe hands periodically as they are working with dirty dishes. However, hands must be properly washed prior to handling clean dishes.

Employees shall properly wash hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles. Common towels and towels used as wiping cloths must not be used for wiping hands.
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Cook was observed chewing gum. Cook discarded gum upon request of inspector.

Employees shall consume food, including gum and candy, only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:

A) box fan in dish area (heavy dust buildup); and
B) can opener blade and holder (food debris) - can opener ran through dish machine during inspection.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use for in-sure equipment, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottles by the ice machine on the north side of the bar were not labeled. Spray bottles contained quat sanitizer (200ppm) and window cleaner. Spray bottles were labeled as to the contents.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-130f Bulk containers of panko, powders, and salt are observed without a proper label. Label contents of bulk containers with common name. Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-140(b) Observed cheese sauce at 95F and chili at 107F in the walk-in cooler. Items were in deep pans and covered. Foods were placed in the walk-in cooler around lunch time. Items were allowed to be reheated to 165 and cooled with an ice bath.   Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. 
750-151(a) Observed turkey in the walk-in cooler with a date of 11/26. Proper date marking was discussed during the inspection - see violation #18.  Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed soiled knife being stored between two soiled sides of prep table and prep freezer on the cookline. Cease storing in-use utensils inbetween pieces of equipment that cannot and/or are not being cleaned and sanitized regularly.   Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed an uncovered pan of bacon being stored beneath the oven in the kitchen. Cease storing items under this oven unless they are protected from overhead contamination. Also, observed garbage bags being used within non-food grade tubs to stored panko. Cease use of garbage bags and use proper food grade lliners for food storage. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-160b Observed employees using same gloves to touch hats and body and then returning to work. Observed employees grab straws with bare hands and no prior handwashing. Discussed handwashing with manager. Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interuption in operations.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed an employee glass, without a proper lid, being stored on the counter between customer cups and soda dispenser. Cease stored employee drinks in food service and equipment storage areas UNLESS the cup is a disposable cup with a lid and a straw. Cup was emptied and removed during the inspection.  Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 REPEAT: The cabinet doors on the southside wait station are observed being repaired with duct tape. Cease use of tape as a repair material. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750-830f  There are old date marking stickers observed on containers in the walk-in cooler, in prep coolers, and in dry storage area. Make sure that labels are removed prior to washing or during the washing process. Dishes with old labels should not be placed in clean and available equipment pile. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b There were two pitiful sani-buckets available for holding washing cloths. One was old and had soiled solution present, the other appeared to be a catch bucket for the drips from the leaking drainpipe noted in violation #28. During the inspection, buckets were emptied, cleaned, and filled with proper sanitizing solution. Keep buckets filled with proper solution and available for use. Discussed the sanitizing of stem thermometers between uses and keeping sani-buckets clean and available. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly

A new gasket was purchased and will be installed. Repair was not completed during the inspection. A spot check on the plumbing will be conducted on Wednesday. All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.
